title: NASA OSTEM Internship — Spring 2027
shortDescription: Paid, mentor-led internships on NASA projects during the Spring 2027 session.
fullDescription: NASA Office of STEM Engagement (OSTEM) internships place college students on real agency projects with NASA mentors. The Spring session typically runs about 15 weeks (mid-January to early May). Most interns receive a stipend based on academic level and session length. Apply through NASA STEM Gateway. U.S. citizenship is required.
eligibility: U.S. citizen; at least 16; college student (undergraduate through graduate) with a cumulative 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale; enrolled at a U.S.-accredited institution.

title: NASA OSTEM Internship — Summer 2027
shortDescription: Paid summer internships contributing to NASA missions under a NASA mentor.
fullDescription: NASA OSTEM Summer internships are typically about 10 weeks (late May through August). Interns work on agency projects in STEM and some non-STEM fields. Apply through NASA STEM Gateway. U.S. citizenship is required. Check individual project listings for location and hybrid options.
eligibility: U.S. citizen; at least 16; college student with a 3.0 GPA; enrolled at a U.S.-accredited college or university.

title: Kaggriculture
shortDescription: Build an AI agent that runs a virtual farm and competes on a live leaderboard.
fullDescription: A Kaggle featured simulation competition. Design, build, and deploy an autonomous agent to manage a virtual farm, trade on a dynamic market, and maximize profit over a simulated season. Entry and team-merger deadline is 23 September 2026; final submission deadline is 30 September 2026 (11:59 PM UTC).
eligibility: Open to Kaggle users who accept the competition rules before the entry deadline. Check Kaggle for prize and team-size rules.

title: ARC Prize 2026 — ARC-AGI-3
shortDescription: Kaggle competition for abstract reasoning systems on ARC-AGI-3 tasks.
fullDescription: ARC Prize 2026 (ARC-AGI-3) is a Kaggle competition on abstract reasoning. Entry and team-merger deadline is 26 October 2026; final submission deadline is 2 November 2026. Winners announcement listed as 4 December 2026. Confirm prize and eligibility on the official Kaggle page.
eligibility: Open to Kaggle users who accept the competition rules before the entry deadline. Review official rules for prize eligibility.

title: Harvard CS50x: Introduction to Computer Science
shortDescription: Harvard's free, self-paced intro to CS covering C, Python, SQL, and web development.
fullDescription: CS50x is Harvard's open-enrollment introduction to computer science. The course covers thinking algorithmically and problem solving with C, Python, SQL, JavaScript, and more. Students earn a verified certificate upon completing all problem sets and a final project. The course is entirely free to audit; a certificate fee applies for the verified credential. Open year-round with a rolling enrolment window.
eligibility: Open to anyone worldwide; no prior programming experience required.

title: Meta Front-End Developer Professional Certificate
shortDescription: Nine-course Coursera certificate covering HTML, CSS, React, and UX fundamentals.
fullDescription: The Meta Front-End Developer Certificate on Coursera prepares students to build interactive web experiences. The nine-course series covers HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React, version control with Git, UX/UI design principles, and interview preparation. Financial aid is available for learners who cannot afford the subscription. Estimated completion is 7 months at 6 hours per week.
eligibility: Open to anyone worldwide. Financial aid available on Coursera.

title: Meta Back-End Developer Professional Certificate
shortDescription: Coursera certificate series covering Python, Django, REST APIs, and databases.
fullDescription: The Meta Back-End Developer Certificate on Coursera teaches server-side programming with Python, the Django framework, REST API design, databases (MySQL), version control, and cloud deployment basics. The nine-course programme includes a capstone project. Financial aid is available. Estimated completion is 8 months at 6 hours per week.
eligibility: Open to anyone worldwide. Financial aid available on Coursera.

title: Google Cybersecurity Professional Certificate
shortDescription: Eight-course Coursera certificate covering networking, Linux, Python, and security tools.
fullDescription: The Google Cybersecurity Professional Certificate prepares learners for entry-level security roles. The eight courses cover security fundamentals, network security, Linux and SQL, Python automation, detection and response, and job-readiness skills. No prior experience is required. Estimated completion is 6 months at 7 hours per week. Financial aid is available.
eligibility: Open to anyone worldwide; no prior IT experience required. Financial aid available.

title: Google Data Analytics Professional Certificate
shortDescription: Eight-course Coursera certificate covering data analysis, R, SQL, Tableau, and spreadsheets.
fullDescription: The Google Data Analytics Professional Certificate teaches the skills needed for an entry-level data analyst role: asking the right questions, data cleaning, analysis, visualisation with Tableau and R, and communicating findings. Estimated completion is 6 months at 10 hours per week. Over 2 million learners enrolled globally. Financial aid available.
eligibility: Open to anyone worldwide; no prior experience required. Financial aid available on Coursera.

title: Google Digital Marketing & E-commerce Professional Certificate
shortDescription: Seven-course Coursera certificate covering SEO, SEM, e-commerce, and marketing analytics.
fullDescription: The Google Digital Marketing & E-commerce Certificate covers foundations of digital marketing, search engine optimisation (SEO), search engine marketing (SEM), social media marketing, e-commerce platforms, and analytics measurement. Estimated completion is 6 months at 10 hours per week. Graduates gain access to the Google Employer Consortium. Financial aid available.
eligibility: Open to anyone worldwide; no prior experience required. Financial aid available on Coursera.

title: Financial Markets
shortDescription: Robert Shiller's free Yale course on financial markets, instruments, and institutions.
fullDescription: Financial Markets is a free Coursera course taught by Nobel laureate Robert Shiller of Yale University. It covers the theory of finance and its real-world applications, including risk management, behavioural finance, insurance, the stock market, debt markets, and financial regulation. The course is free to audit; a certificate fee applies. Approximately 33 hours of content.
eligibility: Open to anyone worldwide. Free to audit; certificate available for a fee.

title: Machine Learning Specialization
shortDescription: Andrew Ng's three-course Coursera specialization on supervised, unsupervised, and RL methods.
fullDescription: The Machine Learning Specialization by Andrew Ng and DeepLearning.AI on Coursera is the updated version of the original Stanford ML course. The three-course series covers supervised learning (regression, classification), advanced algorithms (trees, neural networks), and unsupervised learning with reinforcement learning. All courses use Python and NumPy/scikit-learn. Financial aid available.
eligibility: Open to anyone worldwide; basic Python and high-school mathematics required. Financial aid available.

title: The Odin Project: Full Stack JavaScript
shortDescription: Free, open-source full-stack web development curriculum using JavaScript, Node.js, and React.
fullDescription: The Odin Project is a free, open-source web development curriculum used by hundreds of thousands of learners globally. The Full Stack JavaScript path covers HTML/CSS, JavaScript fundamentals, React, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, and deployment. The curriculum is project-driven and entirely self-paced. No cost, no account required to start.
eligibility: Open to anyone worldwide. No prior experience required.

title: AWS Cloud Practitioner Essentials
shortDescription: Free AWS training course covering core cloud concepts, services, and the AWS Cloud Practitioner exam.
fullDescription: AWS Cloud Practitioner Essentials is a free, self-paced digital course on AWS Training that introduces cloud computing concepts, AWS core services (compute, storage, database, networking), security, pricing, and support. The course takes approximately 6 hours and aligns with the AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner exam objectives. No prior cloud experience is required.
eligibility: Open to anyone worldwide; no prior cloud experience required.

title: MLH Fellowship — Software Engineering & Open Source
shortDescription: Paid 12-week remote fellowship contributing to open-source projects with a structured cohort.
fullDescription: The MLH Fellowship is a 12-week remote programme where students contribute to open-source software used by companies like Meta, GitHub, and MongoDB. Fellows are grouped into cohorts, pair-program with industry engineers, and ship real features. Stipends are provided. Applications open multiple times per year for Spring, Summer, and Fall cohorts.
eligibility: Currently enrolled students or recent graduates (within 12 months). Open globally.

title: GitHub Octernships — Paid Student Fellowships
shortDescription: Paid remote fellowships connecting students in emerging markets with partner companies.
fullDescription: GitHub Octernships connects students in emerging markets (including Pakistan) with partner technology companies for paid, project-based fellowships. Students apply to specific partner companies through the GitHub platform. Projects are typically 3–6 months and completed remotely. GitHub provides career development resources and a community for all Octerns.
eligibility: Currently enrolled students in emerging markets. Check individual partner listings for specific requirements.

title: Google Summer of Code (GSoC) 2027
shortDescription: Paid 12-week remote programme for students to contribute to open-source organisations.
fullDescription: Google Summer of Code (GSoC) is an annual programme that pairs students with open-source organisations for a 12-week paid coding project. Students receive a stipend from Google and work remotely under the guidance of an organisation mentor. GSoC has funded over 20,000 contributors across 800+ open-source projects since 2005. Applications typically open in January each year.
eligibility: 18 years or older; enrolled at an accredited institution or a recent graduate. Open globally.

title: Linux Foundation Mentorship (LFX)
shortDescription: Paid 12-week open-source mentorships on Linux Foundation–hosted projects.
fullDescription: The Linux Foundation Mentorship Programme (LFX) connects students with mentors on projects like Kubernetes, Hyperledger, CNCF tools, and many others. Mentorships run for 12 weeks with paid stipends. Multiple cohorts run each year (Spring, Summer, Fall). Students apply to specific projects on the LFX platform. Open globally.
eligibility: Students 18+; currently enrolled or recently graduated. Open globally.

title: Outreachy Paid Open Source Internship
shortDescription: Paid 3-month remote internship for underrepresented groups contributing to open-source.
fullDescription: Outreachy provides 3-month, paid, remote internships in open source for people subject to systemic bias and underrepresentation in tech. Interns receive a USD 7,000 stipend and USD 500 for networking expenses. Two cohorts run per year (May–August and December–March). Projects span software development, documentation, UX research, and data science across dozens of organisations.
eligibility: People subject to systemic bias or underrepresentation in tech; not currently employed full-time. Open globally.

title: LUMS RISE Research Internship Program
shortDescription: Summer research internship at LUMS's School of Science and Engineering in Lahore.
fullDescription: The LUMS Research Internship for Science and Engineering (RISE) places undergraduate students from Pakistani universities in supervised research projects at LUMS's Syed Babar Ali School of Science and Engineering. Interns work alongside faculty on CS, data science, EE, and physics projects over 6–8 weeks in the summer. Stipends may be available for selected participants.
eligibility: Undergraduate students enrolled at a Pakistani university; strong academic record required.

title: United Nations Volunteers (UNV) Youth Programme
shortDescription: Remote and field-based volunteer assignments for youth with UN agencies worldwide.
fullDescription: The UNV Youth Programme places young professionals (18–29) in volunteer assignments with UN agencies, NGOs, and national partners globally. Assignments cover humanitarian work, development, data, communication, and policy. Online volunteer assignments are available globally, with a living allowance for on-site field assignments. Applications are project-based through the UNV portal.
eligibility: Youth aged 18–29; completed secondary education. Online and field positions available globally.

title: CERN Summer Student Programme
shortDescription: Eight-to-thirteen-week paid on-site programme at CERN for physics and computing students.
fullDescription: The CERN Summer Student Programme provides undergraduate and master's students in physics, computing, engineering, and mathematics the opportunity to work at CERN in Geneva for 8–13 weeks. Students join a CERN group, attend a lecture series, and contribute to experiments and computing projects. A stipend and travel contribution are provided. Applications typically open in December.
eligibility: Enrolled in at least 3rd year of university; studying physics, computing, mathematics, or engineering. Open globally.

title: Microsoft Learn Student Ambassadors (MLSA)
shortDescription: Global student programme for tech leaders to build communities and earn Microsoft certifications.
fullDescription: Microsoft Learn Student Ambassadors (MLSA) is a global programme for university students passionate about technology. Ambassadors host workshops, hackathons, and study jams; earn free Microsoft Azure credits, certifications, and Microsoft 365; and gain access to a global peer network and Microsoft mentors. Applications are open year-round. Pakistani students have a strong presence in the programme.
eligibility: Currently enrolled university students worldwide; English proficiency required.

title: Motive 12-Week Hybrid Engineering Internship
shortDescription: 12-week engineering internship at Motive's Lahore and remote offices for CS students.
fullDescription: Motive (formerly KeepTruckin) is a US-listed technology company with a large engineering hub in Lahore, Pakistan. Their engineering internship programme runs for 12 weeks in a hybrid model, placing interns in product squads working on fleet management, AI, and logistics software. Interns receive a competitive stipend and full-time offer consideration upon graduation.
eligibility: Enrolled in a BS/MS in Computer Science or Software Engineering; strong programming fundamentals.

title: Systems Limited Future Leaders Internship Program
shortDescription: Structured summer internship at Pakistan's largest IT company across engineering, QA, and consulting.
fullDescription: Systems Limited is one of Pakistan's largest publicly listed IT services companies. The Future Leaders Internship places students in teams across software engineering, quality assurance, business analysis, data, and client consulting. Interns work on live client projects and attend structured training sessions. Positions are available in Lahore, Karachi, and Islamabad offices.
eligibility: Enrolled in final 2 years of a BS in CS, SE, or Business at a Pakistani university.

title: UNDP Digital, AI & Policy Global Remote Internship
shortDescription: Remote internship with UNDP on digital transformation, AI policy, and development data.
fullDescription: UNDP (United Nations Development Programme) regularly opens remote internships in its Digital Office, Chief Digital Office, and country bureaus. Interns support work on digital public infrastructure, AI ethics and policy, data analysis for sustainable development goals, and communications. Assignments are typically 3–6 months and are open to students and recent graduates globally, including from Pakistan.
eligibility: Enrolled in a master's or final year of a bachelor's degree; excellent written English. Open globally.

title: Contour Software Developer Internship
shortDescription: On-site developer internship at Contour Software's Karachi and Lahore offices.
fullDescription: Contour Software is a Lahore and Karachi-based subsidiary of Constellation Software (TSX: CSU), one of the world's largest enterprise software companies. Developer interns work on vertical-market B2B software products using .NET, SQL Server, and modern web frameworks. The programme includes mentorship from senior engineers and the possibility of full-time conversion.
eligibility: Enrolled in final 2 years of a BS in CS or SE at a Pakistani university.

title: DevBatch Software Engineering Internship
shortDescription: Lahore-based software engineering internship covering web, mobile, and AI development.
fullDescription: DevBatch is a Lahore-based software house delivering web, mobile, and AI solutions. Their internship programme accepts CS and SE students for placements in frontend, backend, mobile (Flutter/React Native), and AI/ML teams. Interns work on client projects under senior developer supervision. Rolling intake with openings typically in May–June and November.
eligibility: CS or SE undergraduates, 5th semester or beyond, enrolled at a Pakistani university.

title: Canonical Ubuntu Remote Engineering Internship
shortDescription: Fully remote engineering internship at Canonical, the company behind Ubuntu Linux.
fullDescription: Canonical is the company behind Ubuntu, the world's most popular open-source Linux OS. Canonical runs a fully distributed team globally and offers remote engineering internships across areas including kernel development, cloud infrastructure (Juju, MAAS, MicroK8s), security, and web engineering. Interns are paid and treated as regular team members with real deliverables and code merged to production.
eligibility: Enrolled students or recent graduates with strong Linux and programming skills. Open globally.

title: Red Hat Open Source Remote Engineering Internship
shortDescription: Paid remote internship at Red Hat contributing to enterprise open-source projects.
fullDescription: Red Hat, an IBM subsidiary, is the world's leading provider of enterprise open-source software. Red Hat engineering interns contribute to projects like OpenShift, Ansible, Fedora, and RHEL under the guidance of senior engineers. Remote internships are available globally. Interns receive a stipend and are encouraged to submit upstream patches.
eligibility: Enrolled in a BS or MS in CS, SE, or a related field. Open globally with remote positions available.

title: Cubix UI/UX Design & Mobile Internship
shortDescription: Karachi-based UI/UX and mobile design internship at one of Pakistan's top app agencies.
fullDescription: Cubix is a Karachi-based mobile and web development agency ranked among the top app developers globally. Their UI/UX and mobile design internship places students in product design teams creating iOS, Android, and web experiences. Interns use Figma for wireframing, prototyping, and handoff, and work alongside mobile engineers. Monthly stipend provided.
eligibility: Enrolled in a design, CS, or fine arts degree at a Pakistani university. Portfolio required.

title: Human Appeal Global HR, Communications & IT Internship
shortDescription: Remote internship with Human Appeal Pakistan across HR, communications, and IT support.
fullDescription: Human Appeal is an international humanitarian organisation operating in over 25 countries. Their Pakistan office offers internship placements in HR, communications and media, IT support, and fundraising. Interns gain exposure to non-profit operations, humanitarian communications, and organisational management. Placements are typically 3 months with a certificate of completion.
eligibility: Undergraduate students enrolled at a Pakistani university; strong communication skills required.

title: McKinsey & Company Forward Program
shortDescription: Free McKinsey learning programme for students in emerging markets to build business and leadership skills.
fullDescription: McKinsey Forward is a free 8-week online programme designed to develop the problem-solving, analytics, communication, and self-leadership skills that McKinsey looks for in its consultants. It targets students and early-career professionals in emerging markets (including Pakistan). Graduates join an alumni network and receive a certificate from McKinsey. Top performers may be fast-tracked into the McKinsey internship pipeline.
eligibility: Students in penultimate or final year of a bachelor's or enrolled in a master's degree. Open to emerging-market applicants.

title: Unilever Future Leaders League & Internship Program
shortDescription: Unilever Pakistan's flagship summer internship and business case competition for students.
fullDescription: Unilever Future Leaders League (UFLL) is a national business case competition open to all Pakistani university students, feeding into the Unilever Summer Internship. Finalists are offered internship placements across Unilever Pakistan's supply chain, marketing, finance, and HR functions. The internship is 10 weeks with a competitive stipend and the possibility of a graduate-track offer.
eligibility: Penultimate year students at Pakistani universities. Open to all degree programmes.

title: NASA STEM Gateway Challenges
shortDescription: Open engineering and STEM challenge competitions hosted by NASA's STEM Gateway platform.
fullDescription: NASA's STEM Gateway hosts multiple open challenge competitions throughout the year covering engineering design, data science, AI, hardware, and science communication. Challenges are open to students globally (citizenship requirements vary by challenge). Prizes, certificates, and recognition are awarded. Past challenges include app design, data visualisation, and autonomous systems.
eligibility: Varies by challenge; most are open to students globally. Check individual challenge pages on STEM Gateway.

title: MLH Global Hackathon Season
shortDescription: Year-round series of in-person and virtual hackathons run under the MLH official season.
fullDescription: Major League Hacking (MLH) runs an official global hackathon season with hundreds of events annually at universities and online worldwide. Each hackathon spans 24–48 hours. Winners receive prizes, MLH medals, and exposure to tech company sponsors including GitHub, Google, and AWS. Online hackathons are open to students globally including Pakistan.
eligibility: Students 18+; some events accept high-school students. Open globally.

title: Devpost Global AI Agent & Social Good Hackathon
shortDescription: Global online hackathon on Devpost focused on AI agents and social impact applications.
fullDescription: Devpost hosts hundreds of virtual hackathons annually. Their AI Agent and Social Good series challenges teams to build intelligent agents or AI-powered applications that address global challenges in health, education, environment, and finance. Cash prizes, sponsorships, and mentorship from partner companies are offered. Teams of 1–5 can participate from anywhere.
eligibility: Open to students and developers globally; no age restriction on most hackathons.

title: Hashnode Web3 & AI Hackathon Series
shortDescription: Online hackathon series by Hashnode covering Web3, AI, and full-stack application development.
fullDescription: Hashnode runs regular sponsored hackathons open to developers globally. Their Web3 & AI series challenges participants to build decentralised applications, AI-integrated tools, or developer productivity apps. Cash prizes, Hashnode Pro subscriptions, and sponsor credits (AWS, PlanetScale, etc.) are awarded. Participants must publish a project article on Hashnode as part of the submission.
eligibility: Open to developers and students globally; free Hashnode account required.

title: L'Oréal Brandstorm Global Business Case Challenge
shortDescription: Global business case competition where student teams reinvent L'Oréal's beauty business model.
fullDescription: L'Oréal Brandstorm is an annual international business case challenge open to undergraduate and graduate students worldwide. Teams of 2–3 work on a brief set by L'Oréal — typically centred on innovation, sustainability, or digital transformation in the beauty industry — and compete through national rounds to the global final in Paris. The competition develops brand strategy, marketing, and entrepreneurship skills.
eligibility: Undergraduate or master's students; teams of 2–3. Open globally, with national qualifying rounds.

title: Hult Prize Global Social Entrepreneurship Challenge
shortDescription: The world's largest student competition for social entrepreneurship with USD 1 million prize.
fullDescription: The Hult Prize is the world's largest student social entrepreneurship competition, backed by the United Nations. Teams of 4 students develop a scalable social enterprise addressing the annual challenge (focused on issues like food security, health, or climate). Teams compete through campus, regional, and global accelerator rounds. The winning team receives USD 1 million in seed funding. Pakistan has strong on-campus chapters at major universities.
eligibility: Enrolled students at any university; teams of 4. Open globally.
